How to set a Zsh option only if supported
by Evan Hahn, posted Jun 4, 2024, tagged #dotfiles #zsh #guide

I change a bunch of Zsh options. For example, I enable the clobber option:

setopt clobber


However, on older versions of Zsh, I get an error because this is not supported:

setopt: no such option: clobber

To fix this, I wrote a simple function, setopt_if_exists, which only sets the option if it’s supported. Here’s what it looks like:

setopt_if_exists() {

  if [[ "${options[$1]+1}" ]]; then

    setopt "$1"

  fi

}



setopt_if_exists clobber


This takes advantage of Zsh’s options associative array, which has keys for supported options. If the key exists, we set the option. Otherwise, we do nothing.
